textObservations.observation: English retains the homogeneous, isotropic, linear electrostatic point-charge model and excludes boundaries, cavities and leakage. It distinguishes solid elastic constraint forces from the electrical interaction without declaring solid electrostatics impossible. Kerosene/oil are historical context, explicitly not learner experiments with charged or flammable liquids.

The force ratio is tied to the same charges, separation, fixed material state and linear response for the ordinary insulating media under discussion. F0 and F are magnitudes. The SI expression includes vacuum permittivity and relative permittivity, while the explicitly CGSE expression has its distinct coefficient. Absolute charge magnitudes, r squared, epsilon and equation number (8-9) are preserved.

Relative permittivity is explicitly dimensionless and the original dielectric-constant term is identified. Approximate constancy is limited to material state and applicability; independence from temperature, field strength, frequency and direction is not asserted universally. Vacuum epsilon=1 and the later polarization explanation retain the approved meaning. The original appendix remains contextual, with measurement-condition qualifications rather than a promise of an English table embedded here.

Worked-example heading and example 1 are fully English. The 0.03 gram drop, approximate 3x10^-23 gram molecular mass, neutral H2O, ten electrons per molecule, 10^21 molecules and 10^22 total electrons retain approved data and reasoning. Total electrons are explicitly not excess electrons or net charge.

Example 2 specifies stationary same-sign vacuum point charges, 1 kilometer separation and 1 coulomb each, giving repulsion. References (8-2)/(8-8), SI force expression and 9000 newtons remain intact. The rounded Coulomb coefficient is acknowledged. The text is an ideal calculation, not a practical charge-retention experiment.

Example 3 retains identical spheres, common suspension point, two-meter threads, equal same-sign 2x10^-8 coulomb charges and sixteen-centimeter center separation. Light/inextensible threads and point-charge/air assumptions are preserved. 'Any other external forces' is read with the explicitly listed weight, tension and Coulomb force in the following paragraph; it does not remove weight or tension. Weight is downward, tension inward/up along the thread and repulsion horizontally outward. Alpha denotes the angle to the vertical; horizontal and vertical balance are distinct.

Figure 108 and its caption use the supported English alias. Tension is the correct translation of the original elastic-force descriptor, explicitly linked to the thread's elastic force. The exact sine relation, r/(2l), tension formula with r cubed and approximate 3.5x10^-3 newtons are preserved. No small-angle replacement, invented mass, new geometry derivation or image judgment is introduced.

Example 4 retains epsilon=2.1, left negative q1=-3.0x10^-8 C, middle positive q2=1.0x10^-8 C, right positive q3=5.0x10^-8 C, r12=0.4 m and r23=0.6 m. Stationary point charges, homogeneous linear isotropic medium, superposition and boundary exclusions are retained; electrical resultants exclude holding constraints. Pairwise symbols are explicitly magnitudes, not signed components. Opposite-sign attraction and same-sign repulsion, adjacent-distance sum and all pair-force expressions preserve approved meaning.

Both attractive forces on body 1 point right, so magnitudes add. Figure 109 reference/caption are English and the distance between bodies 1 and 3 remains the adjacent-distance sum. F1 expression and rounded 14.5x10^-6 newtons rightward are unchanged in substantive meaning.

Body 2 is attracted by the negative charge to its left and repelled by the positive charge to its right; both contributions point left. Equal-and-opposite interaction partners act on different bodies. The magnitude sum, F2 expression and rounded 14.0x10^-6 newtons leftward are preserved without treating action-reaction partners as cancelling on body 2.

For body 3, F31 is leftward attraction and exceeds rightward repulsion F32 for the supplied data. Opposing magnitudes subtract, giving the unchanged approximate 0.5x10^-6 newtons leftward. Approximate-result qualification remains. Cancellation of internal force pairs in the aggregate vector sum is explicitly distinguished from each body's nonzero electrical resultant.
